originalTitle: US stocks: Londian Wason valued at $2 billion, biggest Chinese debut in New York in over a year
simplifiedContent: A company called Londian Wason, which makes copper foil, has started selling its shares on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). The company is now valued at $2 billion, which is a big deal. To get to this point, Londian Wason raised $94 million by selling more shares than it originally planned. This is the largest initial public offering (IPO) by a Chinese company in the US in over a year, which makes it significant. This means that Londian Wason has made a strong entrance into the US stock market, which could be important for investors to know.

originalTitle: Goldman Sachs ups ETF push, set to acquire Neos Investments for up to $2.25 billion
simplifiedContent: Goldman Sachs, a big investment bank, is buying a company called Neos Investments for up to $2.25 billion. Neos Investments manages about $30 billion in 19 different exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which are like baskets of stocks or bonds that you can buy and sell. This purchase will help Goldman Sachs increase the amount of money it manages in active ETFs to $80 billion. This matters because it shows that Goldman Sachs is serious about growing its business in ETFs, which could be a good opportunity for the company. The acquisition will likely make Goldman Sachs a bigger player in the ETF market.

originalTitle: Nebius shares soar 22% as AI demand powers revenue beat
simplifiedContent: Nebius, a company that provides artificial intelligence (AI) services through the cloud, saw its stock price jump up 22%. This happened because the company made more money than expected, which is known as a "revenue beat". The main reason for this increase was a high demand for AI services, which led to bigger contracts and higher prices. The company's core AI business grew very quickly, increasing six times in size. This suggests that Nebius is likely to continue growing in the future, which is why investors are excited and buying its stock.

originalTitle: Yen Trades Near 160 Level, Keeping Traders on Intervention Watch
simplifiedContent: The value of the Japanese yen is currently stable at around 160 yen per US dollar. This is a important level that investors are watching closely. Investors are waiting to see if the Japanese government or other officials will take action to influence the exchange rate, which is called intervention. This means they might try to make the yen stronger or weaker by buying or selling it. The fact that the yen is holding steady at this level is keeping investors alert and watching for any potential action.

originalTitle: Yen Trades Near 160 Level as Traders Watch for Intervention
simplifiedContent: The Japanese yen is currently being traded at a rate close to 160 yen for every US dollar. This is an important level because investors are waiting to see if government officials will step in to influence the exchange rate. If the yen goes below this level, officials might try to intervene, or get involved, in the market. This means they could try to strengthen the yen by buying it or taking other actions. As a result, investors are paying close attention to see what will happen next.

originalTitle: Cisco stock rises ahead of Q4 earnings as investors focus on AI networking demand
simplifiedContent: Cisco's stock price is going up as the company is about to release its quarterly earnings report. This report will show how well the company did in the last quarter and will give investors an idea of whether Cisco can keep growing. Investors are particularly interested in seeing if Cisco's efforts in artificial intelligence (AI) and networking are paying off. The report will help investors decide if they should keep buying Cisco's stock, which has been doing well lately. The earnings report is important because it will show if Cisco can continue to grow and support its recent stock price increase.
